messages:
alex: Heads up — started seeing p99 tail spikes on prod-dedicated around 11:15 UTC. Baseline for this workload (chat long-context) is p50=18ms p95=52ms p99=420ms but we hit 900-1,200ms for bursts. Noticed `kv_cache` paging activity correlated with spikes.

maria: Which cluster / node? reproducible? any recent config changes?

alex: cluster=dedicated-gpu-6, node=g6-102. Repro is intermittent but strongly correlated with long conversations (~16k tokens) + high conc (60req/s). No config churn last 24h. I grabbed a short profile.

alex: ```
# flamegraph snippet
kv_cache::get -> 45%
kv_cache::evict -> 22%
io::page_out -> 18% (sync)
attn::compute -> 10%
```

ben: hmm io::page_out sync is concerning. Are we hitting swap on host or our own page files?

alex: we use per-shard page files (/mnt/kv_pages). Disk io wait spikes at same timestamp. Example log:
```
[2026-03-16T11:15:02Z] evict: shard=3 candidate=conv_1337 entries=2048 policy=LRU
[2026-03-16T11:15:02Z] page_out: shard=3 file=/mnt/kv_pages/page_3_00012.pf size=4MB duration=120ms
[2026-03-16T11:15:02Z] io_wait: 95ms
```

riley: any difference if you force FIFO vs LRU for that shard? we experimented with FIFO for fragmentation before.

alex: ran a local A/B: LRU on shard 3 gave more evictions and paging but FIFO reduced paging volume. BUT saw a small correctness regression with FIFO: ~0.1% of requests returned garbled token sequences (looks like stale KV indexing). We have a failing assert in integration tests: `assert(kv_lookup(idx).seq_id == expected_seq)` occasionally fails under concurrent evict + write.

maria: oh that sounds like an indexing race. Are we doing atomic swaps for the index table when evicting multiple entries?

ben: current flow is: pick candidates -> mark as evicted -> append page file -> update index map in place. No full atomic swap. Concurrency windows exist if a new write for the same conv arrives while page_out is in flight.

alex: exactly. Repro script attached (small snippet):
```
# repro.py (simplified)
for i in range(200):
  start_long_conv(client, tokens=16000)
  concurrently_submit_updates(client, conv_id)
  sleep(0.01)
```

riley: possible mitigations: 1) pin "active" convs (recently touched) to avoid eviction 2) do index swap atomically + apply pointer vid updates 3) change eviction to segmented-LRU or CLOCK to reduce churn 4) increase batch_eviction_size so fewer page_out ops but larger amortization 5) temporarily rate-limit long-context requests.

eva: for short-term rollouts, can we disable paging (i.e., keep everything in-memory) on the affected nodes? disk io seems to be the p99 culprit. We'll pay memory for a hotfix.

alex: I tested disabling paging for shard 3 — p99 returned closer to normal but memory soared and we risk OOM if sustained. Good for a 1-hour mitigation though.

maria: correctness fix must be atomic index update + a small CAS on sequence ids. Add integration tests that stress concurrent evict+write with randomized timing. Ben, can you pick up the patch?

ben: I'll send a PR that does: build a new index table for the eviction batch, write page files, then atomically swap the pointer to the index table and bump a global generation counter. Readers check generation + seq id. Should close the race. Will also add a histogram metric `kv.eviction.generation_mismatch`.

riley: Also please include the option for segmented-LRU in config. If CLOCK proves simpler and reduces page_outs, we can try it as alternative.

alex: I'll schedule a 5% canary on dedicated cluster after PR. For rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m watch windows. If p99 >650ms or any `generation_mismatch` >0, rollback.

runtime-bot: Deploy scheduled: PR #3421 -> canary 5% at 13:00 UTC. Alerting: `infra.kv.p99_latency`, `kv.eviction.generation_mismatch`

eva: also add a short-term config tweak: reduce `kv.max_cache_entries` from 1.2M to 800k on affected nodes to slow churn while patch lands.

ben: noted. I'll aim to have the PR and integration tests up in the next 3 hours. If anyone wants to help with stress harness, ping me.

maria: thanks team — good triage. Alex can you attach the profiler and the raw host logs to the PR?

alex: will do, uploading flamegraphs and iostat traces now.

ben: quick note — we'll also add stronger assertions to detect token corruption in e2e checks so we catch regressions earlier.

riley: thanks all. Keeping this thread pinned until canary clears. :thumbsup:
